_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) refractory to fludarabine and alemtuzumab.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, multicenter, historically-controlled, fixed-dose (2000 mg for 11 doses) monotherapy trial
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with CLL refractory to both fludarabine and alemtuzumab (double-refractory, DR subgroup, n=59)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response rate (ORR), IRC-determined, as primary analysis
pivotal_trials.n: 154 total patients; primary efficacy double-refractory (DR) subgroup n=59
pivotal_trials.result: In the double-refractory subgroup (n=59), objective response rate of 42% (99% CI: 26%, 60%) with estimated median duration of response of 6.5 months.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were neutropenia, pneumonia, pyrexia, cough, diarrhea, anemia, fatigue, dyspnea, rash, nausea, bronchitis, and upper respiratory tract infections. Infusion reactions occurred in 44% of patients on the day of the first infusion. Of 108 patients with normal baseline neutrophil counts, 45 (42%) developed ≥Grade 3 neutropenia and 19 (18%) developed Grade 4 neutropenia.
target_moa: CD20-directed cytolytic monoclonal antibody; binds to both the small and large extracellular loops of the CD20 molecule, with the Fc domain mediating B-cell lysis via complement-dependent cytotoxicity and antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity.

advisory_committee.vote: Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (May 29, 2009) voted 10 yes; 3 no that the results of Protocol Hx-CD20-406 supported accelerated approval of Arzerra as a single agent for CLL.

description.text: Added new indication: ofatumumab in combination with chlorambucil for previously untreated CLL patients for whom fludarabine-based therapy is inappropriate

citations.quote: - New indication: ofatumumab, in combination with chlorambucil, for the treatment of previously untreated patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) for whom fludarabine-based therapy is considered inappropriate.

description.text: Added extended treatment indication for CLL patients in complete or partial response after at least two lines of therapy for recurrent or progressive disease

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for modifications to the Arzerra indication. The approved indication is: Arzerra is indicated for extended treatment of patients who are in complete or partial response after at least two lines of therapy for recurrent or progressive CLL.

description.text: Added new indication: ofatumumab in combination with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide for relapsed chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new indication: Arzerra in combination with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide for the treatment of patients with relapsed chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL).

description.text: Original approval of Kesimpta (ofatumumab) for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis in adults, including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for the subcutaneous administration of Kesimpta (ofatumumab) injection (20 mg/0.4 mL pre-filled syringe and pre-filled pen presentations) for the treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS), to include clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in adults.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Durable objective tumor responses (overall response rate / duration of response), accepted as a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: The application is based on demonstration of durable objective tumor responses of a clinically meaningful magnitude in patients with CLL that was refractory to both fludarabine and alemtuzumab.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Completion of clinical trial OMB110911 (Phase III randomized trial of ofatumumab plus chlorambucil versus chlorambucil in previously untreated CLL) to verify clinical benefit through a clinically meaningful effect on progression-free survival.

citations.quote: Granting of this approval is contingent upon completion of clinical trials to verify the clinical benefit of ofatumumab, as outlined in your letter of October 6, 2009.

To submit a final report for ongoing clinical trial OMB110911, entitled, "A Phase III Open-label, Randomized, Multicenter Trial of Ofatumumab Added to Chlorambucil versus Chlorambucil Monotherapy in Previously Untreated Patients with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia" which is intended to verify the clinical benefit of ofatumumab through demonstration of a clinically meaningful effect on progression-free survival.

basis.text: Fast Track designation granted in December 2004 for ofatumumab in combination with fludarabine for treatment of previously untreated CLL (note: the monotherapy development program was not part of the Fast Track program).

citations.quote: Ofatumumab received Fast Track designation for the investigation of ofatumumab in combination with fludarabine for treatment of patients with previously untreated CLL to show an improvement in progression free survival as compared with fludarabine therapy in December 2004.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug designation granted March 10, 2009 for chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

citations.quote: The applicant’s January 22, 2009 request for Orphan Drug designation was granted on March 10, 2009.

summary.text: Ofatumumab (Arzerra) received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601.40-46 based on durable objective tumor responses in the double-refractory subgroup of single-arm Study Hx-CD20-406, with required confirmatory trial OMB110911 to verify clinical benefit; the application had Orphan Drug designation (granted March 10, 2009), prior Fast Track designation (December 2004, for the combination program), and was reviewed by ODAC which voted 10 yes/3 no in favor of approval.

citations.quote: As requested in your letter of January 30, 2009, marketing approval of this product is granted under the accelerated approval of biological products regulations, 21 CFR 601.40-46.
The application is based on demonstration of durable objective tumor responses of a clinically meaningful magnitude in patients with CLL that was refractory to both fludarabine and alemtuzumab.
The applicant’s January 22, 2009 request for Orphan Drug designation was granted on March 10, 2009.

Ofatumumab received Fast Track designation for the investigation of ofatumumab in combination with fludarabine for treatment of patients with previously untreated CLL to show an improvement in progression free survival as compared with fludarabine therapy in December 2004.

The majority (10 yes; 3 no) of the ODAC members agreed that the results of Protocol Hx-CD20-406 supported the accelerated approval of Arzerra®, as a single agent, for the treatment of patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

requirement.text: Submit a final report for ongoing clinical trial OMB110911 (Phase III open-label, randomized trial of ofatumumab plus chlorambucil versus chlorambucil in previously untreated CLL) to verify clinical benefit via progression-free survival.

citations.quote: To submit a final report for ongoing clinical trial OMB110911, entitled, "A Phase III Open-label, Randomized, Multicenter Trial of Ofatumumab Added to Chlorambucil versus Chlorambucil Monotherapy in Previously Untreated Patients with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia" which is intended to verify the clinical benefit of ofatumumab through demonstration of a clinically meaningful effect on progression-free survival.

requirement.text: Develop a validated, sensitive, and accurate assay for detection of an immune response (binding antibodies) to ofatumumab.

citations.quote: To develop a validated, sensitive, and accurate assay for the detection of an immune response (binding antibodies) to ofatumumab, including procedures for accurate detection of antibodies to ofatumumab in the presence of ofatumumab levels that are expected to be present in the serum or plasma at the time of patient sampling.

requirement.text: Conduct an assessment of anti-drug antibody (ADA) response to ofatumumab in at least 300 patients, including ofatumumab-treated patients enrolled in OMB110911.

citations.quote: To conduct an assessment of anti-drug antibody (ADA) response to ofatumumab with a validated assay (required in PMR 2) capable of sensitively detecting ADA responses in the presence of ofatumumab levels that are expected to be present at the time of patient sampling. ADA response will be evaluated in at least 300 patients, including ofatumumab-treated patients enrolled in clinical trial OMB110911.

requirement.text: Conduct clinical trial OMB112855, a trial of QTc intervals in at least 12 patients administered ofatumumab.

citations.quote: To conduct clinical trial OMB112855, a trial of QTc intervals in patients who have been administered ofatumumab
The number of patients evaluated for QTc interval changes will be at least 12.

requirement.text: Conduct an assessment of QTc intervals as a sub-trial in clinical trial OMB110911, with at least 50 patients (25 per treatment arm) with evaluable ECG measurements.

citations.quote: To conduct an assessment of QTc intervals as a sub-trial in clinical trial OMB110911. The total number of patients in OMB110911 with evaluable ECG measurements will be at least 50 (25 per treatment arm).
